areas.responsibility: Complete and verify item mutations, validation, persistence, and concurrency safety while preserving the existing server and read path.
Complete pantry interactions, urgent-item presentation, accessible responsive styling, and visible recovery states.
Verify and, if needed, repair the existing importer and instructions against the integrated product; prove the fresh-folder workflow.

contracts.text: All requests are same-origin. An item is {"id": integer, "name": string, "quantity": integer, "unit": string, "expires": "YYYY-MM-DD" or null, "created_at": string}. GET /api/items returns 200 JSON {"items":[item,...]}, sorted by expiry ascending with nulls last; q is a case-insensitive name substring and expiring_within is a nonnegative integer number of days, including expired items and dates through local today plus DAYS, excluding null expiry. Filters combine. POST /api/items accepts name and quantity, with optional unit and expires, and returns 201 JSON item. PATCH /api/items/{id} accepts one or more of those fields and returns 200 JSON item. POST /api/items/{id}/consume accepts {"amount": positive integer} and returns 200 JSON item; an amount exceeding current quantity returns 409 JSON {"error":"..."}. DELETE /api/items/{id} returns 204 with no body. Name must be 1–80 characters after trimming; quantity is a nonnegative integer; unit defaults to an empty string; expires defaults to null and must be null or a real YYYY-MM-DD date. Reject unknown fields, malformed JSON and invalid values with 400 JSON {"error":"..."}; unknown item IDs return 404 JSON {"error":"..."}. The interface displays returned error text and handles network failures. Concurrent consumption is atomic.

pantry.py owns schema initialization, item validation, and database writes. pantry.open_db(path) opens the specified SQLite database, initializes its schema, and returns a connection; each caller owns and closes its connection. pantry.create_item(connection, data) accepts a mapping with name and quantity and optional unit and expires, applies the same validation and defaults as POST /api/items, atomically commits one successful creation, and returns the created item mapping. Invalid item data raises pantry.ValidationError with a human-readable message and leaves no item written; database and I/O failures propagate rather than being treated as invalid rows. The importer converts CSV quantity to an integer, maps an empty expires field to null, calls create_item once per row, and skips conversion failures and ValidationError. The server uses create_item for API creation. Each creation owns its transaction; callers must not wrap create_item in a larger transaction expecting it to remain uncommitted.
web/index.html is served at /; local assets under web/ are served at /web/ with appropriate content types and traversal protection. No runtime network assets or build step.

waves.goal: Complete pantry actions, urgent-item presentation, accessibility and visual quality; verify persistence, concurrency, failure recovery, and the existing importer in the integrated fresh-folder workflow.

answer.why: The approved first wave has an integrated display check. The importer and interface checks that lacked peer files still need integrated evidence. Area commitments retain every accepted handle for ownership; the wave lists only remaining commitments. The shared-pantry agreement specifies initialization, validation, errors, and transaction ownership without changing accepted scope.
